'stirred' means mixed round with a spoon; it does not make pieces
you pour liquids, not solid carrots

solution: 'chopped' means cut into pieces.
chop = cut into pieces

questions.stem: It is ______ to cross the road without looking both ways.

explain.why: 'enjoyable' means pleasant, which does not describe a risk
'tiring' means causing tiredness, not risk
'pleasant' means nice, not what crossing without looking is

solution: 'dangerous' means likely to cause harm.
dangerous = likely to cause harm

questions.stem: The old man walked ______ with the help of a walking stick.

explain.why: 'fast' means quickly, which does not suit an old man who needs a stick
'brightly' goes with light or smiles, not with walking
'speedily' means quickly; a man needing a stick would not walk so

solution: 'slowly' fits an old man who needs a stick.

questions.stem: Ben felt ______ of his sister for winning the first prize.

explain.why: 'ashamed' means embarrassed; winning a prize is not shameful
'afraid of' means scared of; winning a prize gives no reason to fear her
'tired of' means fed up with, which does not fit winning a prize

solution: 'proud of' means pleased about someone's achievement.
proud = pleased with achievement

questions.stem: The test was so ______ that most pupils finished it early.

explain.why: 'hard' means difficult, so most pupils would not finish early
a confusing test would slow pupils down
a difficult test would take longer, not shorter

solution: An 'easy' test lets pupils finish early.

questions.stem: The fireman ______ the child from the burning house.

explain.why: 'delayed' means made late; it does not describe saving the child
firemen do not ignore a child in danger
'blamed' means said it was someone's fault; it does not describe getting the child out

solution: 'rescued' means saved from danger.
rescue = save from danger

questions.stem: I am ______ to my teacher for her help with my spelling.

explain.why: 'angry' does not fit being helped
'ungrateful' means not thankful, the opposite of what help deserves
'afraid' means scared, which does not fit being helped

solution: 'grateful to' means thankful to someone.
grateful = thankful

questions.stem: The ______ of the jungle made the children feel afraid.

explain.why: 'cheer' means happiness, not a cause of fear
'warmth' suggests comfort, not fear
brightness would make them feel safer

solution: Darkness in a jungle is a natural cause of fear.

questions.stem: Our class ______ money to help the flood victims.

explain.why: 'stole' means took without permission, not how a class helps victims
'squandered' means wasted; it does not match helping the victims
'borrowed' means took to give back; it does not help victims

solution: 'collected' means gathered together money to give.
collect = gather

questions.stem: The ______ puppy hid under the bed when it heard the fireworks.

explain.why: 'hungry' does not explain hiding from noise
'mischievous' means playfully naughty; hiding from noise is not that
'proud' does not match hiding

solution: Hiding from loud noise shows the puppy is 'frightened'.
frightened = scared

questions.stem: Although she had won the debate, Priya remained ______ and thanked her teammates for the credit.

explain.why: 'stubborn' means refusing to change one's mind; it is not about humility
'vain' means too proud of oneself; she gives credit to others
'arrogant' means showing too much self-importance; she thanks others instead

solution: 'modest' means not boasting about one's success.
modest = not boastful

questions.stem: The ______ aroma of curry drifted from the hawker stall and made our stomachs growl.

explain.why: 'unpleasant' would not make stomachs growl
'stale' means no longer fresh; a stale smell would not make people hungry
'revolting' means disgusting; it would not make stomachs growl

solution: 'appetising' means making people want to eat.
appetising = making you hungry

questions.stem: The shopkeeper ______ the customer of trying to steal a packet of biscuits.

explain.why: you 'scold someone for' something; 'of' does not follow
you 'blame someone for' something, not 'blame someone of' it
'warned someone of' needs a danger, not a wrongdoing he is said to have done

solution: 'accused someone of' is the correct collocation for saying someone did wrong.
accuse of = say someone did wrong

questions.stem: The students listened ______ as the astronaut described her trip to space.

explain.why: 'idly' means without purpose; it suggests not really listening
'grudgingly' means unwillingly, which does not fit a fascinating talk
'inattentively' means without paying attention, the opposite of the sentence

solution: 'attentively' means paying close attention.
attentively = with close attention

questions.stem: My brother is very ______; he never wastes a single cent on things he does not need.

explain.why: 'lavish' means spending freely, the opposite of never wasting a cent
'extravagant' means spending too much, the opposite of never wasting money
'careless' means not taking care, which does not describe money habits here

solution: 'thrifty' means careful with money.
thrifty = careful with money

questions.stem: The sudden clap of thunder ______ the baby, who began to cry.

explain.why: 'soothed' means calmed; the baby began to cry
'amused' means entertained; a baby who cries is not amused
'entertained' means amused, but the baby cried

solution: 'startled' means gave a sudden shock.
startle = give a sudden shock

questions.stem: The detective examined the room ______, not missing even a single footprint.

explain.why: 'lazily' means without effort; it contradicts the thorough search
'superficially' means only on the surface, so he would miss details
'casually' means without much attention; it contradicts not missing a footprint

solution: 'meticulously' means with great care about details.
meticulously = very carefully

questions.stem: Despite the heavy rain, the runners ______ in finishing the race.

explain.why: 'consisted' says what something is made of; it does not mean kept going
'resisted' means fought against; it does not fit finishing a race
'insisted' goes with 'on', not 'in'

solution: 'persisted in' means kept going despite difficulty.
persist = keep going

questions.stem: The principal's speech was so ______ that several pupils began to yawn.

explain.why: 'amusing' means funny, which keeps people awake
'inspiring' means encouraging, which would hold attention
'thrilling' means very exciting, which would not cause yawning

solution: 'tedious' means long and boring, causing yawns.
tedious = boring and long

questions.stem: Rina felt ______ when her friends forgot her birthday.

explain.why: 'thrilled' means very excited; forgotten birthdays do not cause this
'determined' means set on doing something; unrelated to being forgotten
'curious' means eager to learn; it is not the feeling of being forgotten

solution: 'neglected' means feeling ignored or unimportant.
neglected = ignored

questions.stem: The wooden hut was so ______ that a strong wind could have blown it down.

explain.why: 'spacious' is about size, not strength
'sturdy' means strong, so wind could not blow it down
'ancient' means very old; old things may be strong, so it does not give the result

solution: 'flimsy' means weak and easily damaged.
flimsy = weak and thin

questions.stem: The ______ shopkeeper gave the lost child a sweet and called her mother.

explain.why: 'hostile' means unfriendly; she was kind to the child
'impatient' means unwilling to wait; she took time to help
'unsympathetic' means not feeling for others, but she helped the child

solution: 'compassionate' means showing kindness to someone in trouble.
compassionate = showing sympathy

questions.stem: The fruit seller ______ the apples carefully so that they would not bruise.

explain.why: 'dumped' means dropped carelessly, which would bruise apples
'hurled' means threw hard, which would bruise apples
'scattered' means thrown about, which would not be careful

solution: 'arranged' means put in order with care.

questions.stem: The accountant ______ the figures twice to make sure there were no mistakes.

explain.why: 'ignored' means paid no attention, the opposite of making sure
'guessed' means estimated without checking, the opposite of making sure
'invented' means made up, which would be dishonest here

solution: 'verified' means checked to be correct.
verify = check that something is true

questions.stem: The ______ trail was full of rocks and tree roots, so the hikers moved slowly.

explain.why: 'tidy' means neat; it does not describe a rocky path
'flat' means level; rocks and roots make it uneven
'smooth' means even; rocks and roots make a path uneven

solution: 'rugged' means rough and uneven.
rugged = rough and uneven

questions.stem: The boy ______ the secret to his best friend in a low voice.

explain.why: 'shouted' means said very loudly, not 'in a low voice'
'declared' means stated firmly and openly, not a quiet secret
'announced' means said publicly; a secret is not announced

solution: 'whispered' means spoke very softly, matching 'in a low voice'.
whisper = speak very softly

questions.stem: Mrs Tan was ______ with the class's progress and gave everyone a sticker.

explain.why: 'puzzled' means confused; it would not lead to a reward
'displeased' means not happy; she gave stickers as a reward
'startled' means shocked, not a reason for a reward

solution: 'delighted' means very pleased.
delighted = very pleased

questions.stem: The stray dog looked ______, its ribs showing under its dull coat.

explain.why: 'muscular' means strongly built; visible ribs show thinness
'sleek' means smooth and glossy, which does not fit a dull coat
'plump' means rounded and well fed; visible ribs show the opposite

solution: 'scrawny' means thin and underfed.
scrawny = very thin

questions.stem: Uncle Lim is famous for his ______ service; he never keeps customers waiting.

explain.why: 'grudging' means unwilling, which does not describe quick service
'sluggish' means slow, the opposite of never keeping customers waiting
'casual' means relaxed; it says nothing about speed

solution: 'prompt' means quick and on time.
prompt = quick, on time

questions.stem: The two brothers were ______ over who should wash the dishes.

explain.why: 'whispering' means speaking softly, which does not show a dispute
'rejoicing' means celebrating, which is odd for chores
'chatting' means talking in a friendly way; it does not fit a dispute

solution: 'bickering' means arguing about small matters.
bicker = argue over small things

questions.stem: The magician's trick ______ the audience, who could not guess how it was done.

explain.why: 'bored' means uninterested; people trying to guess are interested
'flattered' means praised too much; it does not explain not guessing
'scolded' means told off; a trick does not scold

solution: 'baffled' means completely puzzled.
baffle = puzzle completely

questions.stem: She spoke ______ about her dream of becoming a doctor, her eyes shining.

explain.why: 'reluctantly' means unwillingly; shining eyes show enthusiasm
'nervously' means with fear; shining eyes suggest joy
'indifferently' means without interest, the opposite of shining eyes

solution: 'passionately' means with strong feeling.
passionately = with strong feeling

questions.stem: The athlete's ______ determination inspired the whole team.

explain.why: 'temporary' means lasting a short time; it could not inspire a team
'hesitant' means unsure, the opposite of firm determination
'inconsistent' means changing, which would not inspire a team

solution: 'unwavering' means steady and never weakening.
unwavering = steady

questions.stem: The match was ______ until Saturday because of the rain.

explain.why: a match 'cancelled until' a date is wrong; cancelled means it will not happen
'repeated' means done again, but the match had not yet been played
'ended until Saturday' makes no sense

solution: 'postponed until' means moved to a later time.
postpone = move to a later time

questions.stem: The minister's ______ remarks about the new policy left reporters unsure whether he supported it.

explain.why: 'hostile' means unfriendly; it does not explain the uncertainty
'emphatic' means forceful and clear, the opposite of leaving people unsure
'forthright' means direct and honest, so reporters would know his view

solution: 'ambiguous' means open to more than one meaning.
ambiguous = unclear in meaning

questions.stem: Her ______ curiosity led her to open every drawer and cupboard in the house.

explain.why: 'fleeting' means short-lived, which would not drive such thorough searching
'halfhearted' means without enthusiasm, the opposite of opening every drawer
'dormant' means inactive, the opposite of her restless searching

solution: 'insatiable' means impossible to satisfy.
insatiable = can never be satisfied

questions.stem: He gave a ______ shrug, as if the outcome of the match made no difference to him.

explain.why: 'sheepish' means embarrassed; it does not mean unconcerned
'ecstatic' means overjoyed, which does not fit 'no difference'
'bewildered' means confused, not unconcerned

solution: 'nonchalant' means calm and unconcerned.
nonchalant = casually unconcerned

questions.stem: The scientist's findings were ______ by later experiments, which proved her theory correct.

explain.why: 'overlooked' means not noticed; later experiments could not prove her theory by being unseen
'contradicted' means said the opposite, but the experiments proved her correct
'postponed' goes with events, not findings

solution: 'corroborated' means supported with further evidence.
corroborate = confirm with evidence

questions.stem: The ______ child clung to her mother's skirt and refused to greet the guests.

explain.why: 'bold' means confident, the opposite of clinging and refusing to greet
'mischievous' means playfully naughty; it does not explain clinging
'inquisitive' means eager to learn; it does not explain refusing to greet

solution: 'timid' means shy and easily frightened.
timid = shy and fearful

questions.stem: After weeks of ______ practice, she finally played the piece without a single error.

explain.why: 'sporadic' means happening now and then, which rarely produces faultless playing
'halfhearted' means without enthusiasm, unlikely to give perfect results
'casual' means relaxed and not serious, too weak to explain a perfect result

solution: 'diligent' means careful and hardworking, which explains the result.
diligent = hardworking

questions.stem: The manager's ______ tone calmed the angry customers.

explain.why: 'patronising' means talking down, which would annoy them more
'sarcastic' means mocking, which would anger them more
'curt' means rudely brief, which would make them angrier

solution: 'soothing' means calming.
soothing = calming

questions.stem: Ali's excuse was so ______ that no one believed it for a moment.

explain.why: a genuine excuse would be true and believed
a convincing excuse would persuade people
'trustworthy' describes a person, and a trustworthy excuse would be believed

solution: 'implausible' means hard to believe.
implausible = hard to believe

questions.stem: The mountaineers had to ______ the dangerous slope before dawn, while the snow was still hard.

explain.why: 'transmit' means send a signal or illness, not cross a place
you transport goods; you do not 'transport a slope'
you transfer objects or people, not a slope

solution: 'traverse' means to cross.
traverse = cross

questions.stem: The old fisherman had a ______ face, lined by years of sun and wind.

explain.why: 'glossy' means smooth and shiny, not lined
'immaculate' means perfectly clean and neat, not lined by wind
'pampered' means spoiled with care, not worn by weather

solution: 'weathered' means worn by exposure to weather.
weathered = worn by weather

questions.stem: The headmaster's stern warning had a ______ effect on the noisy class; not a whisper was heard.

explain.why: 'amusing' means funny, which would not silence a class
'refreshing' means pleasantly new or cooling, which does not fit
'soothing' means comforting; a stern warning does not comfort

solution: 'sobering' means making someone serious.
sobering = making serious

questions.stem: The villagers lived in ______ conditions, with no clean water and barely enough food.

explain.why: 'ample' means plenty, but there is barely enough
'comfortable' means having ease, the opposite of having no water
'prosperous' means wealthy, which contradicts lacking food

solution: 'wretched' means miserable and poor.
wretched = miserable

questions.stem: The tourists were ______ by the grandeur of the ancient temple and fell silent.

explain.why: 'amused' means entertained; it does not explain falling silent
'embarrassed' means feeling awkward, which grandeur does not cause
'irritated' means annoyed, which does not suit admiring grandeur

solution: 'overawed' means filled with wonder.
overawed = filled with wonder

questions.stem: His ______ remarks about her cooking made Mei lose her appetite.

explain.why: 'enthusiastic' means very keen, which would not hurt her
'complimentary' means praising, which would please her
'tentative' means uncertain; it does not explain her lost appetite

solution: 'disparaging' means speaking of something as having little value.
disparaging = belittling

questions.stem: The librarian's ______ gaze made the noisy boys fall silent at once.

explain.why: 'admiring' means full of praise, which would not silence them
'wistful' means sadly longing, which would not silence boys
a 'kind' gaze would not make noisy boys fall silent

solution: 'stern' means serious and strict.
stern = strict

questions.stem: The speaker tried to ______ the angry crowd with a calm and polite reply.

explain.why: 'inflame' means make angrier, the opposite of calm
'ignore' does not fit 'with a calm and polite reply', which is a response
'provoke' means make angrier, which a calm reply would not do

solution: 'pacify' means calm someone down.
pacify = calm

questions.stem: Encouraged by the latest trial, the scientists are ______ that a cure will be found within ten years.

explain.why: 'sceptical' means doubtful; being encouraged does not make people doubtful
'indifferent' means not caring; the scientists are working on a cure and are encouraged
'pessimistic' means expecting the worst; 'encouraged' points to hope

solution: 'optimistic' means hopeful about the future.
optimistic = hopeful

questions.stem: The refugees were ______ with food and blankets by the volunteers.

explain.why: you donate things, not 'donate people with' things; the pattern 'were donated with' is wrong
'contributed' is not used with 'with' in this way
'granted' goes with permission or wishes, and not with 'with food'

solution: 'provided with' is the right pattern for 'given what is needed'.
provide with = supply

questions.stem: Mr Lee is a ______ man who rarely says more than he needs to.

explain.why: 'outspoken' means frank in speaking out, the opposite of rarely speaking
'talkative' means chatty, the opposite of rarely speaking
'sociable' means fond of company, which does not fit someone who says little

solution: 'reserved' means quiet and slow to show feelings.
reserved = quiet

questions.stem: The toddler was ______ by the colourful bubbles and could not look away.

explain.why: 'unnerved' means made nervous, which would make her look away
'disheartened' means discouraged, which would not hold a toddler's gaze
'deterred' means put off, the opposite of not looking away

solution: 'mesmerised' means held completely in attention.
mesmerise = fascinate

questions.stem: The singer's ______ voice filled the hall and brought tears to many eyes.

explain.why: 'hoarse' means rough from a sore throat, which does not bring tears
'monotonous' means dull and unchanging, which would not bring tears
'feeble' means weak, which would not fill a hall

solution: 'haunting' means beautiful in a sad, lingering way.
haunting = beautiful and lingering

questions.stem: The teacher was ______ with first-time offenders, giving them a warning rather than a detention.

explain.why: 'ruthless' means without pity, the opposite of giving a warning
'furious' means very angry, which does not fit a mere warning
'indifferent' means not caring; she did give a warning

solution: 'lenient' means not strict in punishing.
lenient = not harsh

questions.stem: It is ____ to run along the wet corridor.

explain.why: 'missafe' is not a word; 'mis-' means 'wrongly' and does not go with 'safe'
'dissafe' is not a word; 'dis-' does not go with 'safe'
'insafe' is not a word; 'safe' takes 'un-' to mean 'not safe'

solution: 'un-' means 'not', so 'unsafe' means 'not safe'.

questions.stem: Mei Lin ____ the instructions and put the model together the wrong way.

explain.why: 'inread' is not a word
'disread' is not a word
'unread' means not yet read, but she did read them wrongly

solution: 'mis-' means 'wrongly', so 'misread' means 'read wrongly'.

questions.stem: The pupils were punished for ____ the school rules.

explain.why: 'inobeying' is not a word
'unobeying' is not a word; the opposite of 'obey' uses 'dis-'
'misobeying' is not a word

solution: 'dis-' gives the opposite meaning, so 'disobey' means 'not to obey'.

questions.stem: The ____ kites filled the sky at Pasir Ris Park.

explain.why: 'colourment' is not a word
'-ly' makes adverbs, but a noun like 'kites' needs an adjective
'colourtion' is not a word

solution: '-ful' means 'full of', so 'colourful' means 'full of colour'.

questions.stem: The puppy was ____ until the animal shelter took it in.

explain.why: 'homement' is not a word
'hometion' is not a word
'homeful' is not a word

solution: '-less' means 'without', so 'homeless' means 'without a home'.

questions.stem: The principal made an ____ about the new canteen stall.

explain.why: 'announceful' is not a word
'announcetion' is not a word; '-tion' is not added to 'announce'
'announceless' is not a word

solution: '-ment' makes a noun from a verb, so 'announce' becomes 'announcement'.

questions.stem: Please follow the ____ carefully before you start the experiment.

explain.why: 'instructless' is not a word
'instructments' is not a word; the noun uses '-tion'
'instructfuls' is not a word

solution: '-tion' makes a noun from the verb 'instruct', giving 'instruction'.

questions.stem: Which word is formed correctly to mean 'not able to be seen'?

explain.why: 'misvisible' is not a word
'unvisible' is not a word; 'visible' takes 'in-'
'disvisible' is not a word

solution: 'in-' can mean 'not', so 'invisible' means 'not able to be seen'.

questions.stem: Which word means 'to fill again'?

explain.why: 'unfill' is not a standard word and 'un-' would mean to undo
'disfill' is not a word
'misfill' would mean to fill wrongly, not again

solution: 're-' means 'again', so 'refill' means 'fill again'.

questions.stem: Which word is a compound word?

explain.why: 'careless' is made from 'care' and '-less', so it is not a compound
'quickly' is made from 'quick' and '-ly', so it is not a compound
'beautiful' is made from 'beauty' and '-ful', so it is not a compound

solution: 'sunflower' joins two whole words, 'sun' and 'flower'.

questions.stem: Which word is formed by joining 'sun' and 'light'?

explain.why: 'sunslight' adds an extra letter and is not a word
'lightsun' puts the words in the wrong order
'sunlighting' adds an ending that changes the word

solution: Joining 'sun' and 'light' in that order makes 'sunlight'.

questions.stem: Meiyi ran ____ to catch the bus.

explain.why: 'quick' is an adjective, but 'ran' needs an adverb
'quicker' is a comparison, but nothing is compared
'quickness' is a noun and cannot describe how she ran

solution: An adverb describes the verb 'ran', so 'quickly' is correct.

questions.stem: Zhi Wei is a very ____ boy who always tells the truth.

explain.why: 'honesty' is a noun and cannot describe a boy
'honestness' is not the usual word
'honestly' is an adverb, but 'boy' needs an adjective

solution: An adjective is needed before 'boy', so 'honest' is correct.

questions.stem: The boy answered the question ____.

explain.why: 'correctness' is a noun and does not describe how he answered
'correct' is an adjective, but 'answered' needs an adverb
'correction' is a noun and does not describe how he answered

solution: An adverb describes how he answered, so 'correctly' is right.

questions.stem: We should show ____ to our elderly neighbours.

explain.why: 'kindly' is an adverb, but 'show' needs a noun here
'kindful' is not a word
'kinder' is a comparison, but nothing is compared

solution: A noun is needed after 'show', so 'kindness' is correct.

questions.stem: The committee was unable to reach a ____ after the long discussion.

explain.why: 'decisively' is an adverb, but 'a' needs a noun
'decide' is a verb, but 'a' needs a noun
'decisive' is an adjective, but 'a' needs a noun

solution: After 'a', a noun is needed, so 'decision' is correct.

questions.stem: The captain's ____ leadership helped the team win the match.

explain.why: 'decide' is a verb, but an adjective is needed here
'decisively' is an adverb, but 'leadership' needs an adjective
'decision' is a noun, but an adjective is needed before 'leadership'

solution: An adjective describes the noun 'leadership', so 'decisive' is correct.

questions.stem: When the ball came towards him, the goalkeeper reacted ____ and saved the penalty.

explain.why: 'decisive' is an adjective, but 'reacted' needs an adverb
'decision' is a noun and cannot describe how he reacted
'decided' is a verb form, not an adverb

solution: An adverb describes the verb 'reacted', so 'decisively' is correct.

questions.stem: The doctor's ____ helped Mr Tan recover quickly.

explain.why: 'treated' is a verb form, but a noun is needed after 'doctor's'
'treatable' is an adjective, but a noun is needed
'treatful' is not a word

solution: A noun follows 'doctor's', and the noun for 'treat' is 'treatment'.

questions.stem: Which word means 'a person who works for a company'?

explain.why: 'employment' means having a job, not a person
'employer' means the person or company that gives the job
'employable' describes someone suitable for a job

solution: The suffix '-ee' marks the person who receives the action, so 'employee' works for the company.

questions.stem: Which word means 'not honest'?

explain.why: 'mishonest' is not a word
'inhonest' is not a word
'unhonest' is not a word; 'honest' takes 'dis-'

solution: 'dis-' gives the opposite, so 'dishonest' means 'not honest'.

questions.stem: Aiman was so sorry that he went to ____ to his teacher.

explain.why: 'apologetically' is an adverb, but 'to' here needs a verb
'apologetic' is an adjective, but 'to' here needs a verb
'apology' is a noun, but 'to' here needs a verb

solution: After 'to' a verb is needed, so 'apologise' is correct.

questions.stem: The scientist made an important ____ about plastic waste in the sea.

explain.why: 'discoverable' is an adjective, but a noun is needed
'discover' is a verb, but 'an important' needs a noun
'discovering' is a verb form and is not the usual noun here

solution: After 'an important', a noun is needed, so 'discovery' is correct.

questions.stem: The ____ of the new library was completed last month.

explain.why: 'construct' is a verb, but 'The' needs a noun
'constructive' is an adjective, but 'The' needs a noun
'constructively' is an adverb, but 'The' needs a noun

solution: After 'The', a noun is needed, so 'construction' is correct.

questions.stem: The librarian was very ____ and found the book for us.

explain.why: 'help' is a verb or noun, but 'very' needs an adjective
'helping' does not make sense after 'very'
'helpless' means unable to help oneself, which does not describe a librarian who found the book

solution: '-ful' means 'full of', so 'helpful' means 'giving help'.

questions.stem: Which word means 'to understand wrongly'?

explain.why: 'disunderstand' is not a word
'reunderstand' is not a word
'ununderstand' is not a word

solution: 'mis-' means 'wrongly', so 'misunderstand' means 'understand wrongly'.

questions.stem: Which word means 'to arrange again'?

explain.why: 'inarrange' is not a word
'unarrange' is not a word
'dearrange' is not a word

solution: 're-' means 'again', so 'rearrange' means 'arrange again'.

questions.stem: Which compound word means 'a place where aeroplanes land and take off'?

explain.why: 'portair' puts the two words in the wrong order
'airing' is made from 'air' and '-ing', so it is not a compound
'airy' means with plenty of fresh air, and it is not a compound

solution: 'air' and 'port' join to make 'airport'.

questions.stem: Which word is spelt correctly?

explain.why: 'happines' is missing an 's'
'happyness' keeps the 'y'; it changes to 'i' before '-ness'
'happinness' has an extra 'n'

solution: The 'y' changes to 'i' before '-ness', giving 'happiness'.

questions.stem: The class was full of ____ when the Primary 6 camp was announced.
